title: Replace legacy PyPI route smoke with standard autoindex/serve demo
description: The default binary now serves the new human-readable autoindex namespace, so scripts/pypi-mvp-smoke.sh correctly no longer works against it because it targets the retired /r/v1/base64 route. Replace that script with a standard OCI autoindex fixture demo that starts `serve`, browses `/`, retrieves natural file paths, and then extend it with ORAS/CLI CRUD as the demo milestone lands.
design: Do not add a legacy runtime fallback just to preserve the old smoke script. Keep the old pypi_mvp integration tests as migration coverage until the new package-manager acceptance suite replaces them. The replacement script should use REPOSITORY=acme/fixture and an autoindex.v1 manifest with descriptor titles/visibility annotations.
acceptance_criteria: A documented executable smoke script passes against the default release binary, demonstrates root/nested/file/HEAD/redirect/safe-404 behavior, and asserts upstream requests use literal `/v2/acme/fixture/...` paths. No `/r/v1/` or base64 locator appears in the script.
notes: Replaced pypi-mvp-smoke.sh with autoindex-mvp-smoke.sh. Extended pypi_fixture.py --autoindex to synthesize standard autoindex.v1 manifest from corpus PyPI files with descriptor titles/visibility annotations. Smoke now proves root/nested/file GET, HEAD, redirect, safe 404/traversal, literal upstream repository, and no encoded route. Full gates and smoke pass; ORAS/CRUD steps remain in parent demo issue.

title: Run design-doc MVP acceptance demo and release signoff
description: Final gate for the rewritten MVP. Execute the deterministic local fixture demo and the gated live GitHub Packages validation, then verify every design-doc MVP bullet: human-readable autoindex browsing, ORAS push/pull, Let's Encrypt mode, serve lifecycle, autoindex CLI create/update/delete, no significant local package storage, native package-manager consumption, and private GitHub bearer authentication.
design: This is a release gate, not a substitute for implementation tests. Require evidence artifacts or links for each criterion, record any explicitly accepted limitations, and do not declare the design-doc MVP complete based only on unit tests or the old route-map PyPI smoke script. The final demo must be pause-friendly and explain how native file paths map to OCI descriptors.
acceptance_criteria: A signed-off checklist maps each design-doc MVP bullet to passing automated/manual evidence. The local ORAS/autoindex/CRUD demo passes; the live GitHub Packages suite passes with public and private access; TLS/ACME staging behavior is demonstrated; docs and release gates are current; no base64 repository route or runtime route-map dependency remains.

title: Reconcile legacy route-map roadmap with design-doc MVP
description: Review the existing 87-issue Beads roadmap and classify every open issue as superseded, reusable, deferred to a later package-manager milestone, or required by the new autoindex MVP. Add supersession/dependency links and update parent issue notes so contributors do not implement contradictory route-map/base64 architecture.
design: Do not close implementation work that is still useful without documenting the replacement. Supersede or defer route-map/PyPI-specific issues where appropriate; retain low-level streaming/security/OCI work by linking it to new issues. Explicitly create follow-up epics for post-MVP PyPI and DNF CRUD rather than letting those issues appear to block the autoindex MVP.
acceptance_criteria: All open legacy issues have an explicit disposition and no contradictory roadmap item is presented as the current MVP plan. The new epic has a clear critical path and post-MVP boundary. Beads dependency graph has no cycles or orphaned references.
notes: Initial reconciliation completed in migration-matrix.md: conflicting runtime route-map/base64/PyPI behavior is marked replace/remove; bounded transport, digest verification, safe errors, and redaction are marked reusable. Legacy issues still require explicit supersession/defer links.

title: Define and test visibility annotation and path projection contract
description: Choose the minimal OCI annotation/media-type convention that marks an artifact or descriptor as visible in the autoindex namespace, while preserving the descriptor title/path as the served relative path. Define behavior for generic OCI artifacts without the annotation and for manifests with mixed visible/invisible layers.
design: Use namespaced, documented annotations only for visibility and optional metadata. The route itself is always derived from validated descriptor path/title data, never a custom route map. Ensure annotations do not conflict with standard org.opencontainers keys and that ORAS materialization remains useful.
acceptance_criteria: A contract document and tests cover visible objects, invisible objects, mixed manifests, nested paths, path escaping, duplicate paths, and annotation absence. Autoindex listing and GET results are deterministic and match the OCI descriptors exactly.
notes: ADR 0002 now defines io.github.djha-skin.github-oras-packages.autoindex.visible=true and org.opencontainers.image.title as the validated relative autoindex path. Implementation/testing remains.
close_reason: ADR 0002 is the checked-in visibility/path projection contract. Implementation and integration tests remain under the autoindex/OCI work.

title: Implement transparent GitHub Packages OCI auth and repository backend
description: Build the upstream backend contract for GitHub Packages: registry discovery/challenge handling, bearer token exchange, authenticated manifest/blob access, private/public repository behavior, forwarding/refresh rules, and redacted diagnostics. Keep the external registry configurable for local fixtures and future OCI backends.
design: Treat GitHub's native auth flow as a first-class backend rather than assuming a static Authorization header. Parse WWW-Authenticate safely, obtain only appropriately scoped tokens using configured credentials, cache tokens within bounded expiry, retry the original request once on an auth challenge, and never log secrets. Preserve exact repository paths and standard OCI media types.
acceptance_criteria: Unit and integration tests cover public access, private access, bearer challenge/token exchange, expired-token retry, unauthorized response, repository isolation, and secret redaction. The backend works against the local fixture and has a documented live GitHub Packages path.

title: Validate against live GitHub Packages repositories and bearer auth
description: Add a gated live contract suite for actual GitHub Packages/registry.github.com behavior, including public reads, authenticated private reads, token challenge/exchange or whatever GHP natively requires, repository isolation, manifest/blob operations, and ORAS CLI interoperability. Keep secrets out of logs and make the suite opt-in with clear prerequisites.
design: Use ephemeral or dedicated test repositories where possible and token scopes limited to the test. Capture only redacted request observations. Separate deterministic fixture tests from live tests; the latter must prove this is not merely a mock contract. Include a manual/demo path when GitHub policy prevents fully automated cleanup.
acceptance_criteria: With documented GitHub credentials and repository configuration, the live suite can publish a disposable artifact, serve and browse it through the proxy, use `oras pull` and native HTTP clients, exercise private access and bearer auth, and clean up or report cleanup steps. CI never runs it without explicit secrets.

title: Add CLI with serve and autoindex CRUD subcommands
description: Replace the current binary's single-purpose environment-driven listener with a user-facing CLI. Implement `serve` plus an `autoindex` command family for create, update, and delete of individual files/packages or logical entries. Operations must be scriptable, readable by an AI-assisted developer, and must not require users to hand-edit route maps.
design: Define command syntax, exit status, stdout/stderr policy, configuration precedence, repository/reference arguments, and auth input. Autoindex CRUD should produce ordinary OCI objects/metadata through the same service or a publisher client, with no significant package data stored locally. Include dry-run and explicit confirmation behavior for destructive delete operations.
acceptance_criteria: Help output documents `serve`, `autoindex create`, `autoindex update`, and `autoindex delete`. End-to-end tests create an entry, update its bytes/metadata, list it via autoindex HTTP, delete it, and verify absence. The commands use normal filenames and OCI metadata, not route-map editing.

title: Implement OCI Distribution compatibility for ORAS push, pull, manifests, and blobs
description: Make the service a genuine OCI Distribution endpoint usable by the oras CLI for the configured repository: implement the required /v2/ checks, manifest and blob GET/HEAD behavior, upload initiation/chunk/finalization, manifest PUT, and deletion semantics needed by oras push/pull. Preserve bounded streaming and safe authentication forwarding.
design: Follow the OCI Distribution API rather than the current minimal fixture-only subset. Ensure manifests can describe autoindex-visible objects using standard OCI descriptors, annotations, and titles without requiring a route-map layer. Add black-box tests that invoke oras against the local server and inspect/pull the resulting content.
acceptance_criteria: With the server running locally, `oras push` publishes a directory or explicitly named files, `oras manifest fetch` retrieves the manifest, and `oras pull` materializes the expected files. `oras` can HEAD/fetch blobs by digest, and invalid repository/path requests fail safely. No custom route-map is required for ORAS interoperability.

title: Implement read-only human-readable autoindex directory and file serving
description: Build the core HTTP read path required by the design document: browse directories as simple HTML autoindex pages, retrieve files at their natural paths, preserve redirects/trailing slash behavior, support HEAD and ordinary HTTP validators, and expose only annotated/eligible OCI content. Do not use route-map.json or base64 repository locators.
design: Use a filesystem-like logical namespace projected from OCI artifact metadata/descriptors. Directory listings must be deterministic, escaped, and inspectable in a browser. File responses must stream from OCI blobs with bounded memory, verify digest/length, and return safe errors. Keep package-manager-specific semantics out of this layer.
acceptance_criteria: Integration tests browse root and nested directories, discover a file through HTML, GET it at the displayed path, HEAD it, and observe correct not-found/traversal behavior. Tests prove the served URL suffix equals the stored object path and that custom route-map data is not consulted.
notes: Standard OCI autoindex vertical slice now has end-to-end test in tests/autoindex_mvp.rs: autoindex.v1 manifest with visible/invisible layers, natural root/nested/file GETs, HEAD, trailing-slash redirect, hidden object 404, traversal 404, and exact upstream path observations. Added Config.REPOSITORY, path request validation, deterministic escaped HTML, and OciClient::autoindex_snapshot. Legacy PyPI route remains for migration until generic runtime is promoted.

title: Inventory and retire conflicting route-map/PyPI-only architecture
description: Audit the current Rust modules, fixture corpus, smoke scripts, tests, README, and existing Beads roadmap against design-doc.md. Identify which route-map, base64 locator, protocol-specific resolver, and fixture-only assumptions must be deleted, migrated, or retained as lower-level reusable code. Produce a migration matrix before implementation begins.
design: Do not delete working code blindly. Mark each current module as retain, refactor, replace, or remove; identify behavior that can be reused (bounded transport, digest verification, safe errors, auth forwarding) and behavior that violates the new design (custom route-map lookup, encoded repository routes, PyPI-only public API). Link follow-up implementation issues to this inventory.
acceptance_criteria: A repository migration matrix exists, names all conflicting runtime and test surfaces, identifies removal/deprecation points, and links each item to a concrete follow-up issue. No design-doc requirement is left without an owner issue.
notes: Architecture ADRs 0001 and 0002 plus migration-matrix.md are now checked in. Inventory identifies runtime conflicts: routing base64 namespace, route-map OCI snapshot, PyPI proxy, environment-only main, read-only fixture, stale docs, and missing CLI/TLS/live auth. Reusable bounded transport, digest verification, safe errors, and redaction are retained for refactoring.
close_reason: Completed architecture inventory. Checked-in ADRs 0001/0002 and migration-matrix.md classify current routing, OCI, proxy, config, server, CLI entrypoint, fixture, scripts, tests, docs, auth, storage, TLS, and observability surfaces as retain/refactor/replace/remove, with each replacement linked to a Beads issue. No design-doc requirement is unowned.

title: Define and approve new human-readable OCI autoindex URL and repository model
description: Replace the current base64 repository locator and route-map-centered identity model with an explicit, debuggable public URL contract derived from the design document. Decide how a served GitHub Packages repository is selected, how paths are preserved at the end of routes, how OCI /v2 paths coexist with autoindex paths, and how tags/digests/annotations identify objects without introducing a custom route map.
design: Write an architecture decision with concrete examples for public autoindex paths, OCI Distribution paths, repository names containing slashes, tag and digest handling, and security boundaries. Prefer a configured repository/host mapping or an explicit human-readable prefix over encoding repository names in a path. Define the small annotation contract that marks objects visible in autoindex views, while treating object filenames and directory paths as the authoritative route.
acceptance_criteria: A checked-in architecture decision and tests/documentation establish human-readable routes with no base64/base58 segment; every exposed file path matches the stored autoindex path; repository selection is unambiguous; OCI and autoindex namespaces are clearly separated; the design explicitly retires runtime route-map.json requirements.
notes: Ready to begin architecture gate. Must settle human-readable repository selection, OCI/autoindex namespace separation, standard annotation policy, and explicit retirement of base64 locator and runtime route-map before implementation issues are claimed.
close_reason: Accepted ADR 0001 defines one configured literal OCI repository per serve process, human-readable autoindex paths rooted at /, literal /v2/<repository>/ routes, no base64/base58 repository locator, and retirement of runtime route-map.json. ADR 0002 defines the visibility/path projection contract.

title: Rewrite MVP around OCI-backed autoindex server per design-doc.md
description: Reorient the project from the completed fixture-backed PyPI route-map proxy to the design document's actual MVP: a normal autoindex-style HTTP server and OCI/ORAS-compatible gateway over GitHub Packages, with human-readable paths, no base64 repository locator, no custom route-map runtime contract, CLI serving and autoindex CRUD, TLS/Let's Encrypt support, and real GitHub Packages validation. Preserve useful low-level streaming and security work where it fits, but explicitly migrate or retire conflicting route-map/PyPI-only architecture.
design: Use this epic as the dependency root for the design-doc rewrite. First settle the public URL/repository identity and OCI publication model; then implement read-only autoindex/OCI behavior; then CLI CRUD and serve lifecycle; then TLS and live GitHub Packages validation; finally package-manager automation, documentation, and the end-to-end MVP demo. Existing route-map/PyPI issues are historical context and should not be silently treated as satisfying this epic.
acceptance_criteria: A release candidate satisfies every MVP bullet in design-doc.md: autoindex browsing, ORAS push/pull, out-of-the-box Let's Encrypt capability, CLI autoindex create/update/delete, serve command with no significant local package storage, and tested access to actual GitHub Packages including private repositories and bearer authentication. The runtime has no base64 repository routing or route-map dependency, and the final demo exercises native package metadata rather than a bespoke map.
notes: Design doc reviewed on 2026-09-20. Created rewrite roadmap: github-oras-packages-6nr, -e8w, -u03, -7wq, -zxj, -1kk, -us7, -smq, -1av, -csv, -gqv, -z2c, -l61, -4v9, -s5f, -jik, -7t9, -z9g. Architecture decision and migration inventory are the first gates; implementation is not yet started.

title: Implement local PyPI MVP HTTP listener and OCI fixture resolver
description: Advance the fixture-backed PyPI vertical slice by adding the smallest runnable loopback-only HTTP path after runtime configuration. Start from the exact OCI v1 fixture contract and serve prebuilt PyPI Simple HTML and the capturepkg wheel through the proxy. Keep scope limited to anonymous local testing: no uploads, JSON Simple API, other package protocols, live GHCR, or production auth claims.
design: Use the existing strict inbound/routing types, Config, deterministic fixtures, and programmable OCI registry fixture. Add a bounded HTTP listener with graceful shutdown/readiness suitable for a shell smoke test, a fixed-origin OCI manifest/config/route-map/blob resolver with digest/size validation, exact same-repository path construction, and descriptor-bound PyPI route lookup. Preserve mapped HTML/package bytes and stream responses without buffering the whole artifact. Keep the local fixture upstream opt-in and loopback-only.
acceptance_criteria: A checked-in command can start the local registry fixture and compiled proxy on loopback ephemeral ports and run `pip install --no-deps` for capturepkg from `/r/v1/<locator>/pypi/simple/`; the package imports successfully. Unknown projects and missing mapped blobs produce safe failures. Registry observations prove requests stay below the exact configured `/v2/<repository>/` path. No real network or credentials are required; cargo fmt, clippy, workspace tests, release build, and fixture verification pass.
notes: Implemented the fixture-backed PyPI MVP vertical slice. Added validated runtime configuration and loopback-only opt-in, Hyper HTTP/1 listener with health/readiness and graceful shutdown, strict fixed-origin OCI v1 manifest/config/route-map validation, descriptor size/digest checks, credential forwarding/challenge and Retry-After classification, backpressured descriptor-checked blob streaming, exact PyPI route lookup, safe cache/ETag/HEAD/error semantics, and exact-repository isolation. Added pypi_mvp integration coverage for prebuilt HTML/wheel serving, unknown routes, missing blobs, auth canary redaction, and registry path assertions. Added scripts/pypi_fixture.py and scripts/pypi-mvp-smoke.sh; smoke runs release proxy + local fixture, pip install --no-deps, capturepkg import, safe failure, and cleanup. Verified cargo fmt --check, clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --workspace, cargo build --workspace --release, python3 fixtures/verify.py, and scripts/pypi-mvp-smoke.sh. Broader protocol/auth/cache work remains tracked by dependent beads.

title: Deliver a fixture-backed end-to-end PyPI vertical-slice MVP
description:
## Goal
Deliver the first runnable end-to-end vertical slice before completing the other package frontends. PyPI is the selected first protocol because a self-contained PEP 503 HTML page and tiny valid wheel can exercise the complete proxy boundary without the repository-signing/key-distribution complexity required by APT, RPM, or pacman.

## Scope
Run the compiled proxy against a local GHCR-compatible OCI fixture. Publish one strict `oras-packages.v1` layout in a single exact repository (for example `acme/pypi-mvp`) containing a prebuilt `/simple/` page, a prebuilt `/simple/<normalized-project>/` page, and one valid wheel route. A shell-driven test must start the fixture and proxy on loopback-only ephemeral ports, wait for readiness, run `pip install --index-url <proxy-pypi-base>/simple/ <fixture-package>`, assert the installed package can be imported, and clean up every process/temp directory even when the test fails.

The vertical slice must exercise raw route parsing, exact repository preservation, fixed-origin OCI manifest/config/route-map/blob retrieval, byte-for-byte HTML/wheel serving, streamed response transfer, descriptor metadata, and a documented anonymous success flow. It must additionally use a controlled fixture Authorization canary to prove no caller Authorization is sent to an origin other than the configured registry and that the test output does not contain the canary. Private live-GHCR validation remains separately tracked; this slice must not require a real credential.

## Exclusions
Do not make external GHCR, a PAT, a real GitHub account, or public network access part of the test. Do not broaden PyPI compatibility to JSON Simple, uploads, search, project JSON APIs, or proxy-generated/re-written HTML. Do not claim a production private-registry flow until the dedicated GHCR authentication validation is complete.
design:
## Delivery definition

The result is an operator-runnable local MVP, not merely unit/integration coverage. The documented command is a checked-in POSIX shell script (with `set -eu`; use `pipefail` only after selecting a shell that guarantees it) that defaults to a hermetic local fixture and fails closed. It must make no secret-bearing command invocation or output.

### Required flow

1. Generate/load deterministic small fixture bytes: a valid pure-Python wheel and prebuilt PEP 503 HTML with proxy-local canonical links and SHA-256 fragment.
2. Build an OCI image manifest with the exact v1 config and one route-map layer; route-map descriptors reference only blobs in `acme/pypi-mvp`.
3. Start a loopback-only programmable OCI fixture which asserts requests remain below `/v2/acme/pypi-mvp/` and returns the expected manifest/config/map/blob representations.
4. Start the proxy with only the PyPI frontend enabled and its upstream explicitly fixed to the fixture endpoint for this test-only configuration.
5. Run pip in an isolated virtual environment/cache/temp directory against `http://127.0.0.1:<proxy-port>/r/v1/YWNtZS9weXBpLW12cA/pypi/simple/`.
6. Assert installation and `python -c 'import <fixture_package>'` succeed. Assert the fixture saw only expected same-repository OCI calls and did not receive raw client request/credential data beyond approved forwarding semantics.
7. Exercise one controlled failure (such as unknown project or missing mapped blob) and assert a safe response/no proxy panic.
8. Trap EXIT/INT/TERM to stop subprocesses and remove per-test temporary paths. Preserve sanitized failure diagnostics only when explicitly requested.

### Authentication milestone

The initial fixture-backed anonymous install is required. A second fixture invocation may send a non-secret Authorization canary and assert exact forwarding only to the fixture registry plus safe redaction. Do not use a real GHCR credential. The later private GHCR check (`github-oras-packages-nlf.3.4`) and direct relay task (`github-oras-packages-10g.4.3`) remain mandatory before claiming private GHCR support.

### Completion order

This is an integration milestone and remains blocked until its individually scoped foundation/front-end/fixture/auth tasks close. It establishes the earliest executable acceptance command; it does not replace full PyPI coverage or the four-protocol conformance matrix.
acceptance_criteria:
- A documented checked-in shell command runs from a clean checkout and performs a loopback-only fixture-backed `pip install` through the compiled proxy.
- The test uses a real valid wheel, prebuilt PEP 503 HTML, and strict same-repository `oras-packages.v1` OCI layout; no proxy HTML/metadata generation or rewrite occurs.
- The test demonstrates exact decoded repository preservation from public locator through every OCI fixture path and detects a cross-repository attempt.
- The test covers anonymous install success plus one controlled safe failure; it also has a non-secret Authorization-canary assertion that proves fixed-upstream-only forwarding and output redaction.
- The script is deterministic, bounded, cleans up processes/files on success or failure, makes no real-network request, and is suitable for later CI execution.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`, `cargo test`, the release build, and the MVP script all pass.

title: Implement validated immutable layout resolver and snapshot cache
description: Resolve only the fixed oras-packages.v1 manifest for an exact ValidatedRepository, validate the v1 OCI manifest/config/route-map contract, enforce configured resource limits, cache by immutable manifest digest, and expose exact descriptor-bound route lookups. Do not use client-selected tags, map URLs, alternate repositories, or mutable-tag-only cache keys.
acceptance_criteria: A GHCR-compatible fixture proves strict manifest/config/map validation, duplicate/canonical-path rejection, same-repository blob resolution, digest-keyed single-flight snapshot caching, tag-refresh backoff, optional approved-digest enforcement, and bounded failure behavior.

title: Validate direct GHCR authentication forwarding for private package reads
description: Using a dedicated least-privilege test package and credential supplied only through the approved secret mechanism, verify the actual GHCR `/v2/` challenge and read flow relevant to a package-client Authorization header. Determine whether exact direct forwarding succeeds for the selected supported credential form(s), which 401/WWW-Authenticate behavior occurs, and whether a separate broker-mode design is required. Do not record tokens, Basic values, or secret-bearing URLs.
acceptance_criteria: A sanitized test record identifies the GHCR endpoint, request type, accepted credential form or challenge, response status/headers, repository permission prerequisite, and resulting decision. No secret appears in Beads, Git, logs, fixtures, or command history. The OCI auth gateway task is blocked until the result is recorded.

title: Implement CI pipeline for format, lint, unit, integration, and e2e tests
description: Configure CI to run Cargo formatting/lints/unit tests, fixture-backed integration tests, containerized package-manager e2e suites, and the secret/repository invariant gates.
acceptance_criteria: Required checks run from a clean checkout with cached but reproducible dependencies, produce useful failure artifacts, and gate merges.

title: Automate build, quality, supply-chain, and release gates
description: As a maintainer, I need reproducible CI that prevents formatting, lint, test, dependency, artifact, and container regressions from reaching releases.
acceptance_criteria: A clean checkout runs enforced formatting/lints/tests/security checks and builds the release/container artifacts; release provenance and versioning are documented.

title: Create minimal valid package and OCI artifact fixtures
description: Produce or source redistributable minimal wheels/sdists, RPMs, DEBs, pacman packages/databases/signatures, and their agreed OCI manifests/metadata alongside malformed variants.
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures are reproducible, small, licensed/documented, validate against the artifact schema, and include missing/blob-mismatch/bad-metadata cases.
notes: Implemented fixtures/corpus with a reproducible Python standard-library generator and verifier. The corpus contains valid wheel/sdist, RPM v3 with verified header/payload/file digests, DEB, pacman package and sync database, native PyPI/RPM/APT/pacman metadata, a single-layer OCI manifest/config/route map, content-addressed blobs, and malformed invalid-json, duplicate-route, foreign-descriptor, unsupported-version, extra-layer, missing-content, checksum-mismatch, and bad-descriptor cases. Baseline policy is intentionally unsigned and documented; no private keys or credentials are checked in. Added Rust corpus regression tests and documented regeneration/licensing. Verified with Python archive/hash checks, rpm query/checks, cargo fmt, clippy -D warnings, workspace tests, and release build.
close_reason: Implemented and verified deterministic package/OCI fixture corpus, native metadata, malformed cases, generator/verifier documentation, and Rust regression tests. Python archive/hash checks plus cargo fmt, clippy, workspace tests, and release build pass.

title: Implement programmable GHCR-compatible registry test server
description: Build a local test registry or harness with OCI v2 manifest/blob behavior, configurable public/private repositories, `WWW-Authenticate` challenges, expected request assertions, ranges, cache validators, faults, and large streams.
acceptance_criteria: Tests can declare expected method/path/headers and responses; fixture supports all required success/failure/auth/range scenarios without external network access.

It serves exact repository-scoped manifests/blobs, matches method/path/selected headers without retaining sensitive values, supports public/private auth challenges and exact credential checks, HEAD, ETag/304, bounded single ranges, delayed large streams, explicit status faults, and truncated Content-Length responses. Added redaction-focused integration coverage and documented the harness. cargo fmt, clippy -D warnings, workspace tests, and release build pass.

title: Build a GHCR-compatible OCI registry fixture and artifact corpus
description: As a maintainer, I need deterministic public/private OCI registry fixtures and valid package artifacts so every protocol adapter is tested without relying on live GitHub Packages.
acceptance_criteria: The fixture serves manifests/blobs, auth/token challenges, failures, and controlled observability; the corpus includes valid and invalid artifacts for each approved ecosystem.

title: Add automated log/error/telemetry secret-redaction checks
description: Capture logs, errors, metrics, and traces for successful and failed authenticated requests and scan for authorization data, token fragments, signed URLs, or bodies.
acceptance_criteria: A CI check fails when known secret canaries appear in emitted telemetry; diagnostics retain sufficient sanitized correlation information.

title: Create exact OCI repository-name invariant tests
description: Exercise every frontend request shape and assert the outbound OCI `/v2/<repository>/…` path contains exactly the contract-selected repository string, with no case/namespace/prefix/fallback alteration.
acceptance_criteria: Parameterized tests cover positive names plus invalid paths and show no cross-repository request can be induced by package metadata or URL tampering.

title: Test SSRF, traversal, header injection, and redirect defenses
description: Attack the inbound and OCI boundaries with traversal, percent-encoding ambiguity, hostile metadata URLs, control characters, hop-by-hop headers, oversized inputs, redirect responses, and alternate hosts.
acceptance_criteria: Every vector fails before unsafe upstream access or follows the explicit allowlist policy; regression tests prove no credential can cross the allowed upstream boundary.

title: Create cross-protocol credential forwarding and challenge tests
description: For PyPI, RPM, APT, and pacman flows, test anonymous, Basic, and Bearer-compatible requests plus GHCR-style `WWW-Authenticate`, 401, and 403 exchanges using a controlled registry fixture.
acceptance_criteria: Tests assert equivalent incoming authorization is sent only upstream, client-visible status/challenges are correct, proxy-owned credentials are never substituted, and no Authorization value appears in artifacts.

title: Verify credential transparency and exact repository isolation
description: As a security-conscious registry user, I need proof that the proxy forwards my registry credentials only to the configured GHCR-compatible upstream and never rewrites or escapes the repository I requested.
acceptance_criteria: Automated tests cover every protocol and prove auth/challenge relay, credential redaction, exact repository selection, no cross-repository blob access, and upstream-boundary hardening.

title: Validate cross-protocol security, conformance, and release readiness
description: Establish reusable registry fixtures, security regression gates, performance bounds, CI checks, operational documentation, and release criteria for the Rust package-protocol proxy.
acceptance_criteria: All selected frontends have end-to-end evidence, credential/repository invariants pass, automated quality gates are enforced, operator/client docs are published, and a production release checklist is approved.

title: Relay GHCR authentication headers and challenges transparently
description: Forward permitted caller authorization to only the configured registry and faithfully return upstream `WWW-Authenticate`, 401, and 403 semantics without logging or replacing credentials.
acceptance_criteria: Fake GHCR token-challenge tests prove forwarding, challenge relay, anonymous behavior, host isolation, and credential redaction.

title: Implement OCI manifest and blob retrieval operations
description: Implement typed requests for `/v2/<repository>/manifests/<reference>` and `/v2/<repository>/blobs/<digest>`, including HEAD where the contract needs it and descriptor parsing.
acceptance_criteria: A registry fixture confirms GET/HEAD method, encoded reference/digest behavior, accepted media types, descriptor parsing, and streamed blob retrieval.

title: Enforce exact OCI repository-name use in gateway URLs
description: Make repository selection an opaque validated value from the mapping contract and prohibit gateway helpers from changing case, namespace, separators, prefixes, or fallback targets.
acceptance_criteria: Tests assert outbound `/v2/` paths retain the chosen repository string exactly for every supported adapter context and reject cross-repository attempts.

title: Implement authenticated OCI Distribution API gateway
description: As a frontend adapter, I need a reusable client for GHCR-compatible manifest and blob retrieval that sends the caller's credentials and preserves the exact requested repository name.
acceptance_criteria: The gateway constructs verified OCI v2 requests, performs media-type negotiation, streams blobs, relays auth challenges, and has integration tests asserting method/path/header correctness.

title: Implement backpressured upstream request and response streaming
description: Build the async body bridge so large responses move between client and registry with backpressure, no disk spill, and cancellation when either peer disconnects.
acceptance_criteria: A multi-gigabyte-equivalent generated stream demonstrates bounded memory, cancellation releases resources, and body errors are surfaced safely.

title: Enforce v1 HTTP header, validator, and no-range policy

title: Document upstream-boundary threat model and controls
description: Threat-model SSRF, path/header injection, redirects, credential disclosure, response smuggling, decompression/size abuse, and cross-repository blob access; select concrete mitigations.
design:
## Upstream-boundary threat model and controls

### Security objective

The proxy translates package-manager read requests into a very small set of OCI read requests while preserving the caller’s authorization semantics. It must not become an SSRF primitive, a credential relay to an attacker-selected origin, a cross-repository content oracle, a cache that shares private content, or an unbounded CPU/memory/bandwidth sink.

The protected assets are: caller Authorization values and resulting registry tokens; private repository existence and contents; the fixed GHCR upstream identity; publication/route-map integrity; service availability; and credential-safe logs/telemetry. The attacker may control every ordinary client request, package path, headers, encoded spelling, and possibly a publication in a repository to which they can push. The attacker cannot break TLS or SHA-256.

### Trust boundaries

1. **Client → proxy:** untrusted raw request target, headers, optional caller credential, and slow/disconnecting body reader. Package clients are not OCI clients.
2. **Proxy → GHCR:** one configured HTTPS registry origin, initially `https://ghcr.io`, and exact validated OCI `GET`/`HEAD` endpoints only.
3. **GHCR → proxy:** upstream status, headers, manifest/map blobs, payload bytes, challenges, redirects, and errors are untrusted until validated against the contract.
4. **Publisher → route map/native metadata:** publisher controls a mutable layout tag and native package metadata. Its authority is bounded by the exact requested repository; the map cannot select another host/repository, and publisher-side validation must prevent native metadata from pointing package clients elsewhere.
5. **Proxy → observability/cache:** logs, metrics, traces, errors, and caches are lower-trust storage and must not receive secrets or authenticated content in MVP.

### Threats, controls, and required verification

| Threat | Required prevention/detection | Verification evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SSRF or credential exfiltration through `Host`, `Forwarded`, `X-Forwarded-*`, `ns`, map metadata, redirects, absolute URLs, userinfo, IP literals, DNS-selected targets, or alternate ports | Upstream origin is a typed fixed HTTPS configuration (`https://ghcr.io` in v1), with normal hostname/certificate verification. The OCI client builds URI paths from typed validated repository/reference/digest values. It never routes from client headers/query/path, native metadata URLs, `ns`, redirect locations, or map fields. Reject userinfo, plaintext HTTP, non-default origins/ports unless a future explicit config allows them. | Fixture asserts no network request leaves the configured origin for hostile route/map/header/challenge/redirect inputs; DNS/TLS/downgrade/alternate-port cases fail locally with sanitized 502/400 as applicable. |
| Ambiguous or malformed client path selects a different repository or map entry | Match raw target against `/r/v1/<canonical locator>/<protocol>/<canonical path>` before framework normalization; reject query, noncanonical base64url, percent escape, decoded slash/backslash, dot/empty/repeated segments, non-ASCII/control characters, unsupported methods. Exact map match only. | Property/negative tests cover aliases, protocol-looking repository segments, `..`, `%2f`, `%5c`, `%66`, duplicate slash, trailing slash changes, query, fragments, and invalid locators; assert zero upstream requests. |
| Cross-repository manifest/blob access | `ValidatedRepository` is opaque after locator validation. Layout resolver and blob client fetch only `/v2/<same repository>/...`; map descriptors have no repository/URL/tag field. Never expose generic OCI endpoints, tag enumeration, referrers, upload, delete, or client-selected digest/reference operations. | Fake registry records exact path and confirms every map/config/blob request remains under selected repository. Tests attempt map/metadata path manipulation and cross-repository digests. |
| Credential confusion, disclosure, or replay | Accept zero/one valid `Authorization` field. Reject duplicates/malformed values and all URL/query/cookie/form/custom credential substitutes. In `registry-forward`, forward the raw value only to fixed GHCR and never transform Basic↔Bearer, mint, persist, cache, or exchange. Anonymous remains anonymous. | Header tests assert only one unchanged Authorization reaches GHCR, never appears in logs/errors/traces, and is absent from anonymous upstream requests. GHCR direct-auth validation task records only sanitized results. |
| Bearer challenge realm abuse or automatic token brokerage | MVP relays upstream `401` and every `WWW-Authenticate` field unchanged; it does not follow a token realm or retry. A future explicit broker mode must validate fixed registry source, Bearer syntax, HTTPS realm allowlist, expected service, minimal derived pull scope, and same-origin retry before sending a credential to a realm. | Registry fixture sends malicious/multiple Bearer realms/scopes; forwarding mode shows no realm request or retry. Any future broker tests assert allowlist checks and no `offline_token`/refresh-token request. |
| Authorization leaks on redirect or `Location` | Do not automatically follow redirects in MVP; relay permitted 3xx response. Never retain Authorization across an origin change; reject HTTP downgrade and redirect loops. `Location` is never a token realm or repository selector. | Same-origin/cross-origin/downgrade redirect fixture checks no unintended second request and no credential propagation. |
| Client request smuggling/header confusion | Parse with a standards-compliant HTTP server; reject conflicting framing, invalid headers, oversized header count/bytes, and request bodies on read-only routes. Strip hop-by-hop headers plus all headers named by `Connection`; construct upstream `Host`. | CL/TE conflict, duplicate Connection-token, obs-fold/control-byte, oversized header, upgrade, and request-body tests cause local rejection without upstream access. |
| Response smuggling/unsafe upstream headers | Stream only valid upstream response framing through the selected HTTP client. Strip hop-by-hop headers and headers named by upstream `Connection`; do not emit raw upstream `Set-Cookie`, proxy auth, or unsolicited routing headers. Preserve only contract-approved end-to-end OCI/cache/range/status headers. | Upstream fixture injects Connection-scoped headers, duplicate framing, Set-Cookie, arbitrary Location, and malformed header values; output is safe or a sanitized 502. |
| Resource exhaustion: huge manifest/map, decompression bomb, huge blob, slow reader, range abuse, connection flood | Bounded manifest/config/map parse limits, route count/path length/descriptor size limits, global/per-client concurrency limits, body/header limits, connect/read/write/idle deadlines, cancellation propagation, bounded outbound connection pool, and no decompression of OCI/native package bytes. v1 rejects Range rather than proxying undefined multi-range behavior. | Generated huge/invalid JSON, compressed native metadata, slowloris, stalled GHCR, large stream, cancellation, timeout, concurrent request, and Range tests show bounded memory/CPU/file descriptors and no stuck work. |
| Mutable tag rollback/substitution or malicious route map | Resolve fixed `oras-packages.v1`, validate manifest/config/map strictly, cache snapshots by returned immutable manifest digest, and optionally pin an approved digest per repository. Maps only point to same-repository sha256 blobs. Publisher validation checks native metadata targets/checksums/signatures. | Fixture validates rejection of index/additional layers/unknown schema/duplicate routes/map over limit/wrong descriptor; pin rejects changed tag; cache keys include repo and digest. |
| Private-content cache leakage or repo existence disclosure | Disable caching for any request carrying Authorization in MVP. If later enabled, isolate by validated identity and authorization context; never cache headers/secrets. Configurable public/private route policy returns deliberate 404 vs 403 without an upstream probe for malformed/denied routes. | Two-principal fixture proves no authenticated response, ETag, body, or cache entry is visible to another caller; denied/malformed paths make no GHCR request and return configured non-disclosing status. |
| Native package metadata sends client outside proxy or invalidates signatures | Serve mapped metadata byte-for-byte: no link rewrite, recompression, newline change, or signature synthesis. Publisher-side validator ensures every native reference resolves to a canonical same-proxy route, checksum/size fields agree with map descriptors, and required sidecars exist. | Per-protocol fixture includes external URL, `..`, encoded separator, missing sidecar, and checksum mismatch; publisher validator rejects. Valid signed fixture remains byte-identical and client verification succeeds. |
| Logging/diagnostic leak | Observability contract is mandatory before production. Redact Authorization, token responses, token-like query strings, signed URLs, bodies, raw upstream URLs/challenges, and repository data where not required. Logs retain only safe operation/status/size/timing/correlation fields. | Canary secret scan in logs, error bodies, spans, metrics labels, crash/panic reports, and test artifacts fails CI on a leak. |

### Normative upstream policy

* **Origin/TLS:** fixed configured HTTPS origin; verified DNS/TLS hostname/certificate; no plaintext fallback, client proxy override, userinfo, IP literal, arbitrary port, or client-controlled proxy environment setting. Deployment egress policy/firewall must restrict the service to configured origin(s).
* **Methods:** client-facing and OCI-facing v1 operations are GET/HEAD only. No upload, mount, delete, tag listing, catalog, referrer, or token endpoint call in forwarding mode.
* **Request headers:** forward only the one Authorization value (if present) and approved end-to-end semantics (`Accept`, `Range` only when a later range policy permits it, `If-*`, selected `User-Agent`). Drop hop-by-hop, `Host`, forwarding/routing headers, cookies, Proxy-Authorization, and any Connection-nominated header. Proxy generates request IDs itself.
* **Response headers:** retain status and selected end-to-end content/cache/integrity headers from the contract; remove hop-by-hop, cookies, proxy authentication, and Connection-nominated headers. Do not expose an upstream hostname, token realm, token, or raw failure body in a locally generated error.
* **Redirects/challenges:** no auto-follow/retry in MVP. Relay upstream 401 challenges and source-protocol-safe error mapping; local policy/TLS/timeout failures are sanitized 4xx/502/504 with no internals.
* **Caching:** no persistence of credentials/tokens. Disable shared response caching when Authorization exists. Snapshot cache is bounded and stores only validated public layout data keyed by exact repository and immutable manifest digest.
* **Publication trust:** map/config/manifest sizes and schema are validated before use. Registry blob response length must agree with descriptor before a successful complete response; v1 does not promise pre-delivery whole-blob digest verification while streaming.

### Residual risks and deployment prerequisites

Direct forwarding intentionally entrusts the proxy with caller registry credentials for the configured upstream; deployment must use TLS from client to proxy and restrict proxy administrators/process access accordingly. A mutable GHCR publication tag permits an authorized publisher to update or roll back package metadata; use optional manifest-digest pins for higher-control deployments. Package signature/key management remains client/publisher responsibility. The proxy is not a package authorization system beyond forwarding the caller’s credential and optional route allow-list; do not deploy it as a public gateway to private repositories without a tested client-auth/authorization policy.

### Sources

* OCI proxy/redirect authorization boundary and API behavior: https://github.com/opencontainers/distribution-spec/blob/main/spec.md#registry-proxying and https://github.com/opencontainers/distribution-spec/blob/main/spec.md#api
* Distribution Registry Bearer challenge flow: https://distribution.github.io/distribution/spec/auth/token/
* RFC 9110 HTTP semantics: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110
* GitHub Container Registry auth and permissions: https://docs.github.com/en/packages/working-with-a-github-packages-registry/working-with-the-container-registry
acceptance_criteria: Threat model assigns mitigations and verification tests for every identified risk, including TLS verification, host allowlisting, redirects disabled or allowlisted, and request limits.
close_reason: Completed upstream-boundary threat model with trust boundaries, mitigations, verification evidence, normative transport policy, residual risks, and standards sources.

title: Specify credential forwarding and OCI challenge relay
description: Define supported incoming Authorization forms, forwarding rules, handling of `WWW-Authenticate`, bearer-token challenges, anonymous requests, and status propagation for GHCR-compatible registries.
design:
## Authentication contract

### MVP mode: `registry-forward` (the required transparent behavior)

The default and only MVP mode is a transparent registry-forwarding proxy. For package-client requests that map to a permitted OCI read operation, the proxy accepts **zero or one** syntactically valid `Authorization` field and forwards its value byte-for-byte **only** to the configured registry origin, initially `https://ghcr.io`. It does not parse, normalize, transform, substitute, persist, cache, mint, or exchange credentials. In particular, it must never relabel a GitHub PAT as a Bearer token.

An absent header is an anonymous request. A malformed Authorization field or multiple Authorization fields is rejected before upstream access; the proxy must never silently choose one. Credentials in URLs, query strings, cookies, form values, or unapproved custom headers are rejected and must not be converted into Authorization.

`ghcr.io` endpoint viability is an explicit P0 validation task (`github-oras-packages-nlf.3.4`); the proxy must not assume that a particular direct Basic or Bearer form is accepted by a registry endpoint merely because it was accepted by another client flow.

### Required forwarding flow

```text
Package client
  GET /<package-protocol-route>
  Authorization: <caller value>   (optional)
          |
          v
Proxy validates route/repository and fixed upstream origin
          |
          | same Authorization value, only to https://ghcr.io/v2/<exact repository>/...
          v
GHCR-compatible OCI registry
          |
          | 200/206/...  -> relay approved status/headers/body
          | 401 + WWW-Authenticate -> relay unchanged
          | 403/404/429/5xx         -> relay according to protocol error contract
          v
Package client
```

The proxy sends only route-derived OCI reads to the upstream (`GET`/`HEAD` manifests or blobs); it must not offer registry writes, deletes, or client-selected `/v2/` paths. The OCI repository value originates in the separate exact-name mapping contract, not from a client-controlled upstream host, URL, tag, or digest.

### Challenge and status relay

* For a registry `401`, relay the status, relevant body, and **every** `WWW-Authenticate` field value. Do not fabricate a local challenge, collapse multiple challenges, rewrite `401` to `403`, or automatically retry.
* Relay upstream `403`, `404`, `405`, `413`, `416`, `429`, and 5xx status semantics through the source-protocol error mapping. Preserve applicable end-to-end headers, including `Content-Type`, `Content-Length`, `Docker-Content-Digest`, `Docker-Distribution-API-Version`, `ETag`, `Last-Modified`, `Cache-Control`, `Range`, `Content-Range`, `Accept-Ranges`, `Retry-After`, `Warning`, `Link`, and OCI headers.
* Remove hop-by-hop headers: `Connection`, `Keep-Alive`, `Proxy-Authenticate`, `Proxy-Authorization`, `TE`, `Trailer`, `Transfer-Encoding`, `Upgrade`, and every header named by `Connection`. Do not forward client `Host`, `Forwarded`, `X-Forwarded-*`, or `X-Original-*`; construct the upstream Host from fixed configuration.
* Keep an upstream `Location` visible only under the redirect policy. In transparent mode, prefer relaying 3xx responses rather than following them. Never forward Authorization across an origin boundary; reject HTTPS-to-HTTP downgrade and never treat a redirect as a token realm.

### Explicit non-MVP: token broker mode

The Distribution Registry token flow is distinct from forwarding: after a 401 Bearer challenge, a broker would send a caller credential to a token authority, receive a short-lived token, and retry a registry request. This changes the security model and is **not** silently enabled. If product validation proves it necessary for non-OCI package clients, implement it only as an explicit future `registry-broker` mode with a separate approval/design.

A broker must: parse `WWW-Authenticate` as HTTP auth syntax; require the 401 to come from the configured registry; require `service` to equal the configured registry identity; require `realm` to be HTTPS and on a dedicated exact-origin allowlist; derive minimal pull scope from the validated OCI operation; send login material only to that validated realm; retry only the same configured registry; cache nothing by default; and never request offline/refresh tokens. Invalid challenges are relayed, not followed.

### GHCR permission expectations

GHCR supports OCI/Docker image formats. Public package pulls can be anonymous. GitHub documents a classic PAT with `read:packages` for reading private packages (or appropriately authorized `GITHUB_TOKEN` in Actions). The proxy never asserts that a token has a scope; GHCR remains the authorization authority.

### Normative security invariants

1. Caller credentials leave the proxy only for the fixed configured upstream origin in forwarding mode.
2. No client input—including `Host`, `Forwarded`, `ns`, challenge parameters, redirects, metadata URLs, or an archive path—selects a credential destination.
3. No credential or token is recorded in logs, traces, metrics, error text, URLs, disk, or shared caches.
4. Anonymous requests remain anonymous upstream.
5. Every upstream authorization result remains distinguishable to the client; proxy failures use sanitized 502/504 only when no usable upstream response exists.
6. Authenticated responses are not cached or shared in MVP.

### Sources

* OCI Distribution Spec, registry proxying and redirect authorization boundary: https://github.com/opencontainers/distribution-spec/blob/main/spec.md#registry-proxying and https://github.com/opencontainers/distribution-spec/blob/main/spec.md#api
* Distribution Registry token authentication: https://distribution.github.io/distribution/spec/auth/token/
* RFC 6750 Bearer challenge/usage: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6750
* GitHub Container Registry authentication/scopes: https://docs.github.com/en/packages/working-with-a-github-packages-registry/working-with-the-container-registry
* GitHub Packages permissions: https://docs.github.com/en/packages/learn-github-packages/about-permissions-for-github-packages
acceptance_criteria: A sequence diagram and normative rules show credentials are forwarded only to the allowlisted registry and 401/403/challenges reach clients without proxy substitution.

title: Design versioned OCI artifact layout and metadata schema
description: Specify how repository indexes, protocol metadata, packages, signatures, layer descriptors, annotations, media types, checksums, and architecture/release dimensions are represented in OCI.
design:
## ORAS package layout v1

### Scope and trust boundary

Each requested repository exposes a package publication through the fixed, client-inaccessible OCI manifest reference `oras-packages.v1`. This is a **publication index**, not a general OCI proxy: package requests can only resolve static entries declared by a validated route map in the same exact repository. The proxy never enumerates tags, follows client-provided OCI references, requests arbitrary blobs, or rewrites native metadata.

`oras-packages.v1` is a mutable publication tag. In standard v1 operation, an entity allowed to publish to the requested GHCR repository is the publication trust root and updates are expected. The proxy caches every resolved snapshot by the immutable manifest digest returned by GHCR; it never caches only by tag or public path. A deployment may configure a per-repository approved manifest digest. When that pin is present, a tag lookup is discovery only and the proxy serves the layout only if its returned digest equals the pin. No OCI signature/referrer policy is part of v1; adding one requires a separately versioned policy rather than silently treating a mutable tag as signed.

The caller still chooses the exact repository through the canonical locator defined in `github-oras-packages-nlf.2.1`. The layout reference and GHCR host are fixed configuration, not client input. This preserves the prompt’s direct repository-name invariant: `foo` is read only from `/v2/foo/...`, never an alias or proxy-owned repository.

### Layout manifest

Fetch only:

```text
GET|HEAD https://ghcr.io/v2/<ValidatedRepository>/manifests/oras-packages.v1
Accept: application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json
```

The proxy must verify the returned body and headers before parsing:

* HTTP success with `schemaVersion == 2`;
* `Content-Type` and manifest `mediaType` are exactly `application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json` in v1; OCI indexes, Docker manifest lists, and unrecognized representations are rejected;
* the raw response body hashes to the response `Docker-Content-Digest`, which must be a canonical `sha256:<64 lowercase hex>` digest in v1;
* one `config` descriptor and exactly one `layers` entry exist; unknown manifest fields may be retained but must not affect policy;
* descriptor `digest`, `size`, and `mediaType` values are syntactically valid, bounded by runtime limits, and use only `sha256` in v1.

The config descriptor has media type:

```text
application/vnd.github.oras-packages.layout.v1+json
```

Its blob is a strict UTF-8 JSON document, no larger than the configured config limit, with exactly:

```json
{"kind":"github-oras-packages-layout","version":1}
```

The sole layer is the route map and has media type:

```text
application/vnd.github.oras-packages.route-map.v1+json
```

It is a strict UTF-8 JSON document, fetched by its descriptor digest from the **same** `ValidatedRepository`. v1 rejects unknown required schema versions, duplicate JSON keys, duplicate routes, missing fields, invalid JSON number/string encodings, unsupported digest algorithms, oversized documents, and additional layers. The gateway sets a narrow Accept value and does not accept a media-type fallback merely because a registry returns 200.

### Route-map schema

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "routes": [
    {
      "protocol": "pypi",
      "path": "simple/example-project/",
      "descriptor": {
        "mediaType": "text/html; charset=utf-8",
        "digest": "sha256:0123...cdef",
        "size": 1234
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

* `version` is integer `1`; only `version` and `routes` are top-level fields in v1.
* `routes` is an array rather than a JSON object so the implementation can reject duplicate `(protocol, path)` pairs explicitly.
* `protocol` is exactly one of `pypi`, `rpm`, `apt`, or `pacman`.
* `path` is a canonical relative raw path below that protocol’s route root. It contains no leading slash, query, fragment, percent escape, backslash, control character, dot segment, empty segment, or repeated slash. Trailing slash is significant and allowed only where the exact protocol route requires it (for example PyPI Simple pages).
* `descriptor` contains exactly `mediaType`, canonical `sha256` `digest`, and non-negative `size`. It has no repository, URL, tag, manifest, referrer, or alternate-host field. Thus every map entry can only be fetched as `/v2/<ValidatedRepository>/blobs/<digest>`.
* Runtime configuration enforces explicit ceilings for manifest/config/map bytes, route count, route-path length, descriptor size, in-flight streams, and cache storage before allocation or upstream retrieval. The final default ceilings are measured and documented by the performance work; v1 must reject rather than partially load an over-limit map.

The public URL maps exactly as:

```text
/r/v1/<canonical-repository-locator>/<protocol>/<path>
```

The router compares the canonical raw `<path>` with one route-map entry. No globbing, route prefix match, fallback, path normalization, metadata-directed path, or router-generated trailing-slash redirect is permitted. On a match, the proxy issues a same-repository OCI blob GET/HEAD by the descriptor digest; it emits descriptor-controlled `Content-Type` and `Content-Length`, an ETag derived from the digest, and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. It streams payloads under the common transport rules. The v1 policy explicitly rejects Range requests until bounded range behavior is designed and tested.

### Native package metadata and signatures

Native metadata is prebuilt and served byte-for-byte as an ordinary mapped blob. The proxy must not regenerate, alter line endings, inject links, change compression, decompress/recompress, or synthesize a signature. This preserves existing signatures where a client is configured with the publisher’s trusted keys.

Required map entries depend on the configured publication, including:

| Protocol | Required mapped metadata/routes in a v1 publication |
| --- | --- |
| PyPI | `simple/` when used, `simple/<normalized-project>/`, each wheel/sdist route; optional `*.metadata` and `*.asc` only when advertised. HTML uses proxy-local canonical links and SHA-256 fragments. |
| RPM | `repodata/repomd.xml`, every location named by it, `repomd.xml.asc` if the signing policy uses it, and each RPM location named by primary metadata. |
| APT | `dists/<suite>/InRelease` **or** `Release` plus `Release.gpg`, every index variant listed/used by the Release metadata, optional `by-hash` only if published, and the exact `Filename` `.deb` paths named by Packages. |
| pacman | `<repo>.db`, `<repo>.db.sig` if required, mapped package archive names, package `.sig` when required, and `.files`/`.files.sig` only if that feature is enabled. |

A publisher-side validator is required before release: it checks every URL/path named by native metadata resolves to a canonical same-proxy route for the same repository; rejects external schemes/hosts, path escapes, encoded separators, and unlisted targets; verifies protocol checksum fields against mapped descriptor digests/sizes where applicable; and verifies that advertised signatures have corresponding mapped sidecars. This is tracked separately because the proxy cannot safely rewrite signed artifacts to correct an invalid publication.

### Publication and cache lifecycle

Publish in this order: upload all package/metadata/signature blobs; upload the config and route-map blobs; construct and locally validate the manifest; push it by digest; verify manifest and all references are retrievable from GHCR; update `oras-packages.v1` last; then update any optional approved-manifest configuration. A failed or incomplete publication must not update the discovery tag.

The proxy performs bounded, single-flight tag refreshes and caches validated snapshots under `(ghcr.io, exact repository, manifest digest)`. It keys route lookups and blob cache entries by at least `(exact repository, manifest digest, protocol, path)` or descriptor digest with repository/digest context, never merely by a public path or mutable tag. It uses refresh backoff for GHCR failures and never treats a stale/failed tag lookup as permission to switch repositories.

### Integrity and limitations

Descriptor size and digest constrain what may be requested, but digest verification before sending the first byte would require buffering/spooling the whole object. For a small streaming MVP, validate the manifest/map/config and descriptor syntax/size before transfer, request immutable GHCR blob-by-digest over verified TLS, and enforce observed length. Do not claim proxy-side whole-blob hash verification until a later bounded verified-cache design is implemented. Package-manager metadata hashes/signatures remain end-to-end client protections.

### Sources

* OCI Distribution API endpoint namespace, manifest/blob retrieval, redirect/proxy guidance: https://github.com/opencontainers/distribution-spec/blob/main/spec.md
* OCI Image Manifest representation: https://specs.opencontainers.org/image-spec/manifest/
* ORAS custom config/artifact guidance: https://oras.land/docs/how_to_guides/manifest_config/ and https://oras.land/docs/concepts/artifact/

It emits neither Accept-Ranges nor Content-Range and does not implement multipart/206/416 behavior until bounded single-range streaming is separately designed and tested. See github-oras-packages-nlf.2.3 for the normative HTTP mapping.

title: Specify exact backing-repository selection invariant
description: For every frontend route, define the path/config component that names the backing repository. It must be used in upstream `/v2/<repository>/…` requests unchanged: no prefixing, namespace insertion, fallback, case transformation, or aliasing.
design:
## Exact backing-repository selection invariant

### Rule

For every package request, the requested backing OCI repository is carried by a **canonical opaque repository locator** in the public proxy URL. The locator decodes to the exact ASCII repository string and that exact string is used as the OCI repository namespace. There is no alias-to-repository mapping, prefix, suffix, default/fallback repository, namespace insertion, case transformation, or lookup by a secondary name. Therefore a request for repository `foo` results only in OCI requests under `/v2/foo/...`; a request for `acme/widgets` results only in `/v2/acme/widgets/...`.

A deployment may have an allow-list that accepts or rejects a requested repository as an authorization boundary, but an allow-list entry may only equal the requested canonical repository string; it cannot map `foo` to another repository.

### Public URL grammar (v1)

```text
GET|HEAD /r/v1/<repository-locator>/<protocol>/<canonical-protocol-path>

repository-locator := unpadded RFC 4648 base64url encoding of the exact ASCII OCI repository string
protocol           := pypi | rpm | apt | pacman
```

The locator prevents an ambiguous slash boundary between multi-segment OCI repository names and package-protocol paths. It is a reversible transport encoding, **not** a repository-name rewrite or an alias. The proxy must decode it once, require canonical unpadded base64url spelling (re-encoding produces exactly the supplied locator), and validate the decoded repository before any route-map or upstream lookup. It must reject padding, percent escapes, query strings, fragments, non-ASCII decoded bytes, invalid UTF-8, empty values, decoded `/`/backslash ambiguities outside normal repository segment separators, dot segments, repeated separators, control characters, and values outside the configured GHCR-compatible repository subset.

For v1, the accepted repository subset is one or more slash-separated, lowercase ASCII segments matching `[a-z0-9]+(?:[._-][a-z0-9]+)*`; an implementation must apply a bounded total length and segment count. This is a strict admission check, not normalization: `Foo`, `foo/`, `foo//bar`, `foo/../bar`, `%66oo`, or a locator whose decoded value does not re-encode byte-for-byte is rejected rather than transformed. Any broader GHCR naming support requires an explicit compatibility update and fixture coverage.

The resulting repository is held in a typed `ValidatedRepository` value. Only the OCI gateway can turn it into a URI, by joining already validated ASCII segments as:

```text
https://ghcr.io/v2/<exact decoded repository>/manifests/<validated-reference>
https://ghcr.io/v2/<exact decoded repository>/blobs/<validated-digest>
```

No generic URL concatenation, URL supplied by package metadata, request `Host`, `Forwarded`, `X-Forwarded-*`, `ns`, query field, manifest layer, redirect, or client-provided OCI path can alter the host or repository. The host is a separate fixed configuration value, initially `ghcr.io`.

### Protocol examples

| Requested OCI repository | Locator | Client-facing request | Required OCI repository path prefix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `foo` | `Zm9v` | `GET /r/v1/Zm9v/pypi/simple/example-project/` | `/v2/foo/` |
| `acme/rpms` | `YWNtZS9ycG1z` | `GET /r/v1/YWNtZS9ycG1z/rpm/repodata/repomd.xml` | `/v2/acme/rpms/` |
| `acme/debs` | `YWNtZS9kZWJz` | `GET /r/v1/YWNtZS9kZWJz/apt/dists/stable/InRelease` | `/v2/acme/debs/` |
| `acme/arch` | `YWNtZS9hcmNo` | `GET /r/v1/YWNtZS9hcmNo/pacman/acme.db` | `/v2/acme/arch/` |

Client configuration points to the appropriate protocol base: PyPI `.../r/v1/<locator>/pypi/simple/`; DNF `.../r/v1/<locator>/rpm/`; APT `.../r/v1/<locator>/apt`; and pacman `.../r/v1/<locator>/pacman/`. The protocol suffix and canonical path determine only the package artifact route; neither selects a different OCI repository.

### Request matching rules

* Accept only `GET` and `HEAD`; reject every other method before map lookup.
* The public router matches the raw request target according to the fixed grammar. It rejects query strings, decoded slash/backslash, dot segments, repeated slashes, path parameters, and non-canonical percent encoding. The proxy must run before any frontend layer that silently normalizes those forms.
* Each protocol has its own strict route-map namespace below the protocol segment. A package client cannot escape its namespace by using slash encoding, alternate spellings, or `..`.
* A valid protocol path still authorizes no OCI operation by itself. It must match an exact validated entry in the immutable layout route map for this same `ValidatedRepository`.

### Error policy

Malformed locator, invalid repository spelling, unsupported protocol, noncanonical path, unknown route, or an allow-list denial produces a local safe not-found/invalid-route response without contacting GHCR. The downstream status/body mapping is specified by `github-oras-packages-nlf.2.3`; logs must retain no raw Authorization value. Public deployments may choose 404 for allow-list denials to avoid existence disclosure.

### Scope and source

OCI Distribution defines the repository as the `<name>` namespace in `/v2/<name>/...` endpoints and defines invalid/unknown name errors; it does not make a client path delimiter safe for this proxy. This contract deliberately uses a canonical transport locator to preserve direct repository identity without ambiguous parsing. Source: https://github.com/opencontainers/distribution-spec/blob/main/spec.md#endpoints and https://github.com/opencontainers/distribution-spec/blob/main/spec.md#error-codes.

### Tests required

The gateway test suite must assert byte-for-byte equality between the decoded repository string and the repository portion of every outbound OCI request for all four examples. Negative tests must cover aliases/prefixes/fallbacks, case changes, percent encoding, encoded separators, dot segments, repeated separators, an invalid locator, a protocol-looking repository segment, client Host/Forwarded injection, and cross-repository blob attempts.
acceptance_criteria: Examples for every supported protocol show input requests and byte-for-byte identical selected OCI repository strings; invalid registry names have documented rejection behavior.

title: Specify supported package-client protocol variants

design:
## Compatibility Matrix (initial contract)

The initial release supports **exactly four** package types: PyPI, RPM, Debian/APT, and Arch/pacman. Every route below is relative to a configured per-repository public base URL. The canonical external routing convention and the rule that selects the backing OCI repository remain the dedicated P0 work in `github-oras-packages-nlf.2.1`; that work must preserve the repository string unchanged in OCI `/v2/<repository>/…` requests.

| Package type | Initial client floor / CI policy | Required discovery and metadata routes | Required archive routes | Initial exclusions / decision boundary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PyPI | `pip >= 24`; CI must pin exact test image/distro versions. | `/simple/` and `/simple/<normalized-project>/`, trailing-slash canonicalization. Serve PEP 503-compatible HTML first; respond `text/html`, one project link at root and one distribution link per project. Distribution links include `#sha256=<hex>`. JSON Simple API content negotiation is a separately tracked enhancement, not an MVP requirement. | Descriptor-bound wheel and sdist links generated from the project page; optional `*.metadata` and `*.asc` only when OCI metadata advertises them. | No upload API, XML-RPC, JSON project API, search API, provenance, or attestations in MVP. |
| RPM | `dnf5` is the supported initial RPM client; CI pins exact image/version. DNF4/YUM/zypper are unclaimed until explicitly tested. | `repodata/repomd.xml`, then every metadata object named by its `location` entries. At minimum require `primary`; serve `filelists`, `other`, `comps`, `updateinfo`, modules, or deltas only if declared in approved scope/artifact layout. | The RPM locations advertised by validated primary metadata, mapped to immutable descriptor-bound routes. | No metalink/mirrorlist; no modularity, updateinfo, delta RPM, group, or optional metadata compatibility promise unless explicitly enabled. Repository signing is carried pre-signed/pass-through or separately decided—never silently re-signed. |
| Debian/APT | `apt >= 2.x`; CI pins exact Debian/Ubuntu image and APT version. | `dists/<suite>/InRelease` as primary signed metadata; support `Release` plus `Release.gpg` for clients that use detached signatures. Serve declared `dists/<suite>/<component>/binary-<architecture>/Packages` index compression variants, initially `Packages.gz`; optional `Sources`, translations, Contents, by-hash, extra architectures and compressions require scope expansion. | Validated `Filename` routes (normally `pool/.../*.deb`) referenced by Packages, with matching Size and SHA256 fields. | No unauthenticated repository mode in production. Initial signing policy is pass-through of OCI-carried, pre-signed APT metadata; proxy-held signing keys require a separate approved design. |
| Arch/pacman | `pacman >= 6`; CI pins exact Arch image and pacman version. | The configured sync repository database `<sync-repository>.db`, plus `<sync-repository>.db.sig` when signature policy requires it. Serve `<sync-repository>.files` and `.files.sig` only after an explicit file-database scope decision. | Descriptor-bound `.pkg.tar.*` package archive names listed in the sync database, plus detached package signatures only when artifact policy includes them. | No AUR protocol, build service, repo-add API, or database generation in MVP. Pass through repository/package signatures; do not synthesize signatures. |

## Shared HTTP rules

* All package metadata and archive retrievals are GET/HEAD only. The shared transport preserves approved validators and archive range semantics and forwards configured registry credentials only to the allowlisted OCI upstream.
* A route may resolve only descriptors declared by validated metadata for the same selected repository. Client-provided paths, URLs, registry hosts, manifest references, and blob digests must not select arbitrary OCI content.
* Existing/reported upstream authorization failures and `WWW-Authenticate` challenges are relayed according to the shared authentication contract. Missing/invalid metadata and missing archives map to the source protocol’s documented 4xx/5xx behavior without exposing registry internals.
* CI must pin exact client image digests/versions in the later end-to-end suite. The listed client floors are the initial public compatibility boundary, not an unbounded claim of compatibility.

## Authoritative references

* PyPA Simple Repository API: https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/simple-repository-api/ (normalized project routes, valid HTML, per-file anchors, hash fragments, content negotiation).
* pip `--index-url` documentation: https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/cli/pip_install/
* DNF5 metadata documentation: https://dnf5.readthedocs.io/en/latest/misc/caching.7.html (mandatory `repomd.xml` and `primary`; optional metadata types).
* rpm-md schemas: https://github.com/rpm-software-management/rpm-metadata
* Debian APT archive-signing guidance: https://manpages.debian.org/testing/apt/apt-secure.8.en.html (Release/InRelease/Release.gpg).
* Arch `pacman.conf(5)`: https://man.archlinux.org/man/pacman.conf.5.en (Server and signature settings).
* Arch `repo-add(8)`: https://man.archlinux.org/man/repo-add.8 (sync database archive format).

## Follow-on work

`github-oras-packages-nlf.1.3` must capture sanitized wire fixtures from the selected pinned client images, including authentication challenges, cache validation, range retrieval, missing metadata, missing archive, and invalid-signature cases. The artifact-layout, signing, and repository-routing tasks must turn the per-repository base URL concept into a versioned, testable contract before an adapter is implemented.
acceptance_criteria: A compatibility matrix maps each selected client operation to HTTP routes, required metadata, status/error semantics, and minimum tested versions.

## Decision
The initial release supports exactly four package types: PyPI, RPM, Debian/APT, and Arch/pacman. No fifth protocol is required or implied.

## Rationale
The project owner confirmed that “five” in the prompt was a typographical error. Limiting scope to the four named ecosystems makes the compatibility and OCI artifact contracts testable.

## Alternatives Considered
1. Infer an unstated fifth ecosystem: rejected; the owner confirmed none is required.
2. Count YUM/DNF separately from RPM: rejected; they are RPM repository clients/protocol variants, not an additional package type.
3. Count APT separately from Debian: rejected; APT is the client/protocol for Debian packages, not an additional package type.
