title: Define credential-safe observability and error policy
description: Specify structured log fields, metric labels, traces, errors, and diagnostic switches that never record authorization data, private repository names when avoidable, signed URLs, or response bodies.
design:
## Credential-safe observability and error policy

### Mandatory boundary

Every observability sink—structured logs, access logs, traces/spans, metrics/exemplars, error responses, health/debug endpoints, panic hooks, crash reports, support bundles, and third-party exporters—MUST receive only a typed allowlisted `SafeEvent`. Proxy code MUST NOT serialize or format a complete request/response, `HeaderMap`, URI, body, `Debug`/`Display` error, error chain, environment, configuration, or arbitrary user string. Redaction happens before any sink or sampling decision; downstream collectors are not a redaction boundary.

All accepted strings are length-bounded and control-character-sanitized before JSON encoding to prevent log injection. Raw client/upstream data remains only in process memory for the duration required to handle the request.

### Permitted default log and trace fields

| Field | Allowed value |
| --- | --- |
| `timestamp` | proxy-generated UTC RFC 3339 timestamp |
| `level` | fixed enum `ERROR`, `WARN`, `INFO`; `DEBUG` only under controlled debug mode |
| `event` | fixed enum such as `request.complete`, `request.rejected`, `upstream.complete`, `translation.failed`, `upstream.unavailable`, `redaction.applied`, `panic` |
| `request_id` | cryptographically random proxy-generated opaque identifier |
| `service.name`, `service.version`, `build_id` | static build metadata only |
| `protocol`, `operation`, `route_class` | fixed enums/templates only, never a path; examples: `pypi`, `manifest_get`, `package.metadata` |
| `status_code`, `upstream.status_code` | numeric status only |
| `outcome`, `failure_class` | fixed enums only |
| `duration_ms`, `request_bytes`, `response_bytes`, `attempt` | bounded numeric values |
| `upstream` | fixed identifier `ghcr`, never host/URL |
| `auth.present` | Boolean only—never scheme, scope, subject, token length, or validity detail |
| `repo_visibility` | trusted local-policy enum `public`, `private`, or `unknown` only |

Default logs use versioned structured JSON. Trace attributes/events use the same allowlist. Metrics use a stricter low-cardinality subset only: protocol, fixed operation, outcome, status class, fixed upstream label, and numeric histograms/counters. Metric labels and exemplars MUST NOT include request/trace ID, repository/package/version/tag/digest, URL/path/query, client address, User-Agent, error message, authorization state, raw status text, or a derived identifier. Exemplars are disabled in MVP.

Repository identity is omitted by default. If a time-limited incident requires correlation, an explicitly enabled log-only `repo_corr` may be `HMAC-SHA-256(rotating_telemetry_key, canonical_repo_id)` truncated to at least 128 bits; it is disabled by default, never a metric label, rotates at least daily, and is retained only for the incident window. Raw or globally stable repository hashes are prohibited.

### Absolute exclusions

The following MUST NOT appear in any observability sink or client-visible locally generated error, in whole or in part:

* `Authorization`, `Proxy-Authorization`, `Cookie`, `Set-Cookie`, token-service responses, session IDs, PATs, Basic/Bearer values, OAuth access/refresh tokens, passwords, API keys, private keys, signing keys, CSRF/nonces, certificate private material, or a hash/fingerprint/prefix/suffix/length of such values;
* raw `WWW-Authenticate` challenge values except while forwarding the required upstream header directly to the client—it is not logged or copied into a local diagnostic;
* request/response bodies, native package metadata, OCI manifests/map/config, blobs, upstream error body/status text, package content, or body snippets;
* full URLs, raw paths, query strings, fragments, `Location`, `Referer`, `Origin`, `Host`, User-Agent, client address, internal DNS/address, repository identity/package coordinate/tag/version/digest, upload identifier, or metadata-derived URL;
* environment variables, command arguments, configuration values, mounted files, source locations, backtraces, memory/core dumps, and formatted third-party errors.

`Authorization` values never enter a metric, trace attribute, exception, request ID, cache key, URL, test snapshot, or support bundle. It is only retained as the raw header value necessary to send to the one configured upstream in `registry-forward` mode.

### Client errors and request correlation

The proxy creates a random opaque `request_id` at ingress; it is the sole client-visible correlation identifier (`X-Request-ID`) and may be logged. It contains no time, host, repository, identity, token, trace data, or sequence. Client-supplied request/correlation IDs are discarded or represented only by a boolean `client_correlation_supplied`; they are never authoritative or forwarded upstream.

A locally generated error contains only the status/protocol response semantics, a fixed safe code when needed, a constant generic title (for example, `Request could not be completed.`), and `X-Request-ID`. It never contains raw upstream bodies/headers, upstream endpoint/realm, repository/package identity, parser/TLS diagnostics, stack trace, or credential outcome. The error-mapping contract (`github-oras-packages-nlf.2.3`) determines status/header interoperability; this policy constrains all body/detail content.

If W3C Trace Context is enabled later, validate its syntax/length but start a new local security boundary trace and a fresh outbound GHCR context. Always discard `baggage`; discard client `tracestate`; do not expose trace/span IDs to clients or metric labels. Automatic HTTP instrumentation is disabled unless it is configured not to capture headers, URLs, queries, bodies, or exception text.

### Debug, health, panic, and support behavior

* Production defaults to INFO; debug is disabled. A deployment-time access-controlled change may enable DEBUG but it adds only fixed state names, timings, counts, and parser categories. It can never relax these exclusions, and it must be time-limited. A `observability.debug_changed` event records only fixed actor/reason classes, not config values.
* Health/readiness returns status plus static build version and a boolean safe-debug state only. It never reveals configuration, upstream URL, repository, cache keys, credentials, or connectivity diagnostics.
* Replace the default Rust panic hook with a safe event containing only `event=panic`, timestamp, request_id if present, static build ID, uptime, and a fixed panic category/code-location fingerprint. It never prints panic payload/message, source path, backtrace, environment, arguments, request context, or memory data. Production core dumps and automatic crash uploads are disabled; any exceptional forensic artifact needs separate encrypted, access-controlled, expiring handling.
* Support bundles use a separately reviewed exporter that only emits this allowlist; `kubectl`/container logs and third-party error SDKs are not assumed safe.

### Required CI safety gates

1. **Golden-sink test:** success, malformed input, 401 challenge, 403/404, timeout, malformed upstream, cancellation, retry, redaction, and panic paths. Capture stdout/stderr, logs, trace exports, metrics, client errors, and crash payloads. Assert all are allowlist-conformant.
2. **Canary test:** inject distinct unique canaries into Authorization (Basic/Bearer), cookies, query/path, repository/package name, body, upstream error, Location, Referer, User-Agent, environment, command arguments, and panic payload. Scan every sink for exact, URL-encoded, base64, and truncated variants; any occurrence fails CI.
3. **Fuzz/property test:** arbitrary untrusted headers/paths/bodies/error strings/control characters must produce bounded valid JSON/fixed enums and no upstream string reflection.
4. **Header/body regression:** unknown headers, authorization/proxy authorization, cookies, bodies, Location, Referer, and formatted errors never appear even in debug mode.
5. **Privacy/equivalence:** two private repositories with equivalent outcomes yield the same default telemetry/client error shape except random request ID and bounded timing; no repository-existence oracle is introduced by local errors.
6. **Trace and panic tests:** inbound baggage/tracestate/correlation canaries are neither exported nor forwarded; panic output matches only the safe schema.
7. **Static/config gate:** fail direct `println!`, `eprintln!`, `dbg!`, arbitrary tracing fields, `Debug`/`Display` of HTTP/error types in proxy paths, automatic HTTP capture of headers/URL/body, core dumps, or exporter configuration that collects environment/locals by default.

### References

* OWASP Logging Cheat Sheet—data to exclude, sanitization, controlled logging changes, and verification: https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Logging_Cheat_Sheet.html
* RFC 9700 OAuth 2.0 Security BCP—access tokens are sensitive and reverse proxies must sanitize security-relevant headers: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9700
* RFC 6750 Bearer Token Usage: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6750
* RFC 9457 Problem Details—security-vetted error detail: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9457
* W3C Trace Context privacy considerations: https://www.w3.org/TR/trace-context-2/
acceptance_criteria: A redaction specification includes positive and negative examples plus automated checks for credentials in logs, telemetry, and error responses.
close_reason: Completed typed allowlist observability, secret exclusions, repository privacy, safe error/correlation/debug/panic policy, and required canary/fuzz/CI gates.

title: Map OCI failures and HTTP cache semantics to package protocols
description: Define how absent manifests/blobs, invalid layouts, digest mismatches, registry 401/403/404/5xx responses, ETags, Last-Modified, and range behavior are exposed to clients.
design:
## HTTP failure, validator, cache, and range contract (layout v1)

### Boundary and response construction

The proxy is the HTTP origin for package clients, not a pass-through OCI Registry API. It serves only a canonical package route that exactly matches the validated v1 route map for the requested exact repository. It emits a package-protocol-safe response from typed local/upstream outcomes; it never placeholds a package/metadata route with OCI JSON, an upstream error body, redirect target, token realm, registry URL, or parser diagnostic.

Every generated response includes the safe request correlation header required by the observability policy. Locally generated error bodies use a fixed generic representation and contain no repository/package/OCI identity. Native mapped metadata and artifacts are exact bytes: no on-the-fly content encoding, decompression/recompression, link rewriting, or content transformation. Successful exact-byte responses include `Cache-Control: no-transform` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.

### Outcome table

| Typed condition | Downstream response | Headers/cache | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Canonical GET route exactly maps to a validated descriptor and the same-repository OCI blob is available | `200 OK`, descriptor-controlled `Content-Type` and exact `Content-Length`; byte stream | ETag/cache rules below | Only successful map entry is a package representation. |
| Canonical HEAD route maps to an available descriptor | Same status and representation headers as GET, no body | Same ETag/cache rules; descriptor `Content-Length` | HTTP HEAD parity. |
| Unsupported method | `405 Method Not Allowed` | `Allow: GET, HEAD`; `Cache-Control: no-store` | v1 is read-only. |
| Malformed locator, unsupported protocol, noncanonical/escaped/query route, deny-list/allow-list refusal, or no exact map entry | local `404 Not Found` (or a fixed configured invalid-route equivalent) | `Cache-Control: no-store`; generic body | Do not query GHCR for malformed/unknown routes; 404 avoids path/repository existence disclosure. |
| Selected repository/layout tag is absent upstream (`404`) before any route map is available | local `404 Not Found` | `Cache-Control: no-store`; generic body | No published package layout exists. Do not use OCI body. |
| Valid map entry but its descriptor blob is absent upstream (`404`) | local `502 Bad Gateway` | `Cache-Control: no-store`; generic body | Published layout is broken; it is not a client-missing route. |
| Manifest/config/map is invalid, unsupported, exceeds a configured limit, has conflicting duplicate paths, or fails its own required descriptor validation | local `502 Bad Gateway` | `Cache-Control: no-store`; generic body | The invalid artifact came from the upstream publication; clients must not receive a partial or synthesized package representation. |
| A mapped blob’s observed completed length contradicts its descriptor, or a transport/integrity check fails before a response can be completed | local `502` if no payload was committed; otherwise abort the downstream transfer and mark it failed | `no-store`; never send a synthetic success/error body after partial bytes | v1 streams from immutable blob-by-digest but does not falsely promise pre-delivery whole-blob hashing. |
| OCI `401 Unauthorized` while fetching layout or mapped content | relay `401` | Relay every upstream `WWW-Authenticate` field needed by the `registry-forward` contract; `Cache-Control: no-store`; safe generic body | Caller credentials are forwarded to fixed GHCR as required by the product. Do not perform a token exchange or log the challenge. |
| OCI `403 Forbidden` | relay `403` | `Cache-Control: no-store`; safe generic body and only contract-approved end-to-end headers | GHCR remains authorization authority. A deployment may later select a non-disclosing policy for public routes, but v1 does not transform a real upstream 403 into a misleading success. |
| OCI `429 Too Many Requests` | `503 Service Unavailable` | Relay syntactically valid `Retry-After` if present; otherwise omit; `no-store` | The registry, not this package client, imposed the limit. Proxy-local client limits use `429` separately. |
| OCI 5xx or malformed upstream response | local `502 Bad Gateway`; use `503` only for a specifically recognized temporary upstream condition | A valid upstream `Retry-After` may be preserved for 503; `no-store`; generic body | Avoid exposing upstream response/status text while expressing gateway availability. |
| Connect/read/write timeout before usable upstream response | `504 Gateway Timeout` | `Cache-Control: no-store`; generic body | Distinguish timeout from a readable upstream failure. |
| Proxy local concurrency/rate limit before upstream | `429 Too Many Requests` | Proxy-generated valid `Retry-After` when known; `no-store`; generic body | This is the only v1 use of client-facing 429. |

The proxy preserves required package-route content headers and selected end-to-end semantic headers only after validation: `Content-Type`, `Content-Length`, ETag, Last-Modified when allowed below, Cache-Control, `Content-Range`/`Accept-Ranges` only when a future range policy allows them, and `Retry-After`. It strips hop-by-hop headers, headers named by `Connection`, cookies, proxy authentication, raw `Location`, and raw upstream error headers/bodies. The authentication contract is the narrow exception for forwarding upstream `WWW-Authenticate` on a real 401; that field is neither logged nor synthesized.

### Validators and cache controls

The mutable `oras-packages.v1` tag means a public package route might be rebound by a later publication. Therefore v1 takes a deliberately conservative cache policy even for version-looking archive filenames:

* **Anonymous successful mapped representation:** `Cache-Control: public, max-age=0, must-revalidate, no-transform`. A strong ETag is exactly the mapped descriptor digest, quoted, for example `"sha256:<64 lowercase hex>"`. This allows normal conditional revalidation without allowing an intermediary silently to retain stale publication state.
* **Any request carrying Authorization:** `Cache-Control: private, no-store, no-transform`, regardless of whether the resulting content would otherwise be public. The proxy does not store or share authenticated responses in v1. Downstream clients may retain their own package cache outside HTTP shared-cache semantics, but proxy response reuse is disabled.
* **Errors and negative results:** always `Cache-Control: no-store`.
* **Last-Modified:** v1 omits it unless a later layout schema supplies a publisher-authoritative timestamp with explicit semantics. It MUST NOT be invented from proxy fetch/cache time, OCI tag observation, or request time.
* **PyPI JSON extension only:** if a future version supports both HTML and JSON Simple API representations, emit `Vary: Accept` and a representation-specific ETag. HTML-only v1 does not emit Vary solely for an ignored Accept preference.

On an exact current representation, honor `If-None-Match` using the strong descriptor ETag. A matching GET or HEAD returns `304 Not Modified`, no body, and the applicable ETag/Cache-Control/Content-Type metadata. If `Last-Modified` is ever emitted, support `If-Modified-Since` only then; `If-None-Match` takes precedence. If correct validator handling cannot be provided for a route, omit validators rather than return an incorrect 304.

### Range and HEAD policy

V1 does **not** implement byte-range delivery. On a request containing `Range`, it ignores the Range field and returns the complete `200` representation; it does not emit `Accept-Ranges` or `Content-Range`, and it does not synthesize multipart responses. This is an intentional conservative HTTP behavior until bounded single-range streaming/caching is designed and tested. Range is also ignored for HEAD. The earlier layout phrase “rejects Range” is clarified by this policy: the feature is unavailable, but a valid client request receives full representation semantics rather than a misleading 416.

HEAD is supported for every mapped GET route. It evaluates routing/auth/layout as GET would and sends the same successful or error status and applicable headers, except no message body. The proxy does not probe a map entry with a client-selected OCI HEAD; the request still resolves only the fixed layout/map descriptor.

### Protocol-specific application

| Protocol | Success and error constraints |
| --- | --- |
| PyPI | Serve canonical PEP 503 HTML routes byte-for-byte as mapped. Project pages carry the publisher’s proxy-local file links and SHA-256 fragments; fragments never arrive at the proxy. The route map includes the exact trailing-slash Simple paths; slashless paths are not redirected in v1 and are treated as noncanonical. Distribution and optional metadata/signature sidecar routes use the same exact-map/error policy. JSON/content negotiation is outside HTML-only MVP. |
| RPM/DNF | Serve `repodata/repomd.xml`, every exact referenced metadata path, optional signature sidecars, and exact RPM paths. A missing map path is 404; a missing blob referenced by validated repodata is 502. Never rewrite/compress metadata or substitute error text under RPM/XML routes; repository checksum/signature verification sees the bytes published. |
| Debian/APT | Serve exact `InRelease`, or `Release` plus `Release.gpg`, declared index compression paths, optional by-hash only when mapped, and exact `Filename` `.deb` paths. A signed/checksum-listed route with a broken upstream descriptor is 502, never a successful error page. Release signatures/checksums remain the source of package trust; HTTP ETags are an optimization only. |
| pacman | Serve exact `.db`, database signature, enabled `.files` variants, package archive, and package signature paths. Preserve archive/signature bytes. No pacman-specific OCI error body/status emulation is promised beyond this generic contract. |

### References and explicit non-goals

* HTTP GET/HEAD, conditional, range, status, and validator semantics: RFC 9110 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110
* HTTP cache handling, especially authenticated-response reuse: RFC 9111 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9111
* OCI blob/manifest GET/HEAD, 404, range recommendation, and 429 Retry-After: https://github.com/opencontainers/distribution-spec/blob/main/spec.md
* PyPI Simple API: https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/simple-repository-api/
* DNF repository configuration/security: https://dnf.readthedocs.io/en/latest/conf_ref.html
* APT transport cache options and apt-secure: https://manpages.debian.org/testing/apt/apt-transport-http.1.en.html and https://manpages.debian.org/testing/apt/apt-secure.8.en.html
* pacman repository/database/signature configuration: https://man.archlinux.org/man/pacman.conf.5.en and https://man.archlinux.org/man/repo-add.8.en

Out of v1: OCI API exposure, uploads/deletes, automatic OCI redirect following, token brokerage, multi-range/multipart delivery, on-the-fly compression, heuristic Last-Modified, stale-if-error metadata, PEP 691 JSON negotiation, and ecosystem-specific retry/status emulation beyond the mapping above.
acceptance_criteria: The contract maps each upstream class to source-protocol status/body/header behavior without information leakage and records caching requirements per client family.
close_reason: Completed typed HTTP status, cache, validator, HEAD, and conservative Range contract for immutable descriptor-mapped package representations.

title: Publish artifact-layout examples and validation fixtures
description: Create small synthetic OCI layouts and expected frontend output examples for the agreed schema so adapters and test fixtures share one source of truth.
design:
## Layout v1 contract examples and validation-fixture matrix

This record is the architecture-side fixture contract. The executable fixture corpus is implemented by `github-oras-packages-efi.2.2`; it must use actual byte hashes, valid package formats, and valid signatures where the protocol policy requires them. Symbolic digests below are only identifiers in this design record and MUST NOT be copied into a real publication.

### Canonical fixture repository and public bases

The common synthetic publication uses the exact OCI repository:

```text
acme/fixture
```

Its canonical unpadded base64url public locator is:

```text
YWNtZS9maXh0dXJl
```

All protocol client bases are therefore:

```text
https://proxy.example.invalid/r/v1/YWNtZS9maXh0dXJl/pypi/simple/
https://proxy.example.invalid/r/v1/YWNtZS9maXh0dXJl/rpm/
https://proxy.example.invalid/r/v1/YWNtZS9maXh0dXJl/apt
https://proxy.example.invalid/r/v1/YWNtZS9maXh0dXJl/pacman/
```

Every layout/config/map/blob fetch in this fixture is constrained to `/v2/acme/fixture/...`; no external repository, hostname, tag, URL, or referrer appears in the route map.

### Valid OCI envelope (structural fixture)

The normal fixture is a single OCI image manifest returned by:

```text
GET /v2/acme/fixture/manifests/oras-packages.v1
Accept: application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json
```

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 2,
  "mediaType": "application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json",
  "config": {
    "mediaType": "application/vnd.github.oras-packages.layout.v1+json",
    "digest": "sha256:<actual-config-digest>",
    "size": 48
  },
  "layers": [
    {
      "mediaType": "application/vnd.github.oras-packages.route-map.v1+json",
      "digest": "sha256:<actual-route-map-digest>",
      "size": "<actual-route-map-size>"
    }
  ]
}
```

The config blob is exactly the canonical UTF-8 JSON:

```json
{"kind":"github-oras-packages-layout","version":1}
```

The executable fixture must calculate its byte length/digest, use canonical `sha256:<lowercase hex>` descriptor spelling, set the matching upstream `Docker-Content-Digest`, and include no additional layer/index/list representation.

### Valid route-map skeleton

The executable route map must use this exact shape and substitute actual descriptor values:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "routes": [
    {"protocol":"pypi","path":"simple/","descriptor":{"mediaType":"text/html; charset=utf-8","digest":"sha256:<pypi-root>","size":<n>}},
    {"protocol":"pypi","path":"simple/capturepkg/","descriptor":{"mediaType":"text/html; charset=utf-8","digest":"sha256:<pypi-project>","size":<n>}},
    {"protocol":"pypi","path":"packages/capturepkg-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl","descriptor":{"mediaType":"application/octet-stream","digest":"sha256:<wheel>","size":<n>}},

    {"protocol":"rpm","path":"repodata/repomd.xml","descriptor":{"mediaType":"application/xml","digest":"sha256:<repomd>","size":<n>}},
    {"protocol":"rpm","path":"repodata/primary.xml.gz","descriptor":{"mediaType":"application/gzip","digest":"sha256:<primary>","size":<n>}},
    {"protocol":"rpm","path":"packages/capturepkg-1.0.0-1.x86_64.rpm","descriptor":{"mediaType":"application/x-rpm","digest":"sha256:<rpm>","size":<n>}},

    {"protocol":"apt","path":"dists/stable/InRelease","descriptor":{"mediaType":"application/pgp-signature","digest":"sha256:<inrelease>","size":<n>}},
    {"protocol":"apt","path":"dists/stable/main/binary-amd64/Packages.gz","descriptor":{"mediaType":"application/gzip","digest":"sha256:<packages-gz>","size":<n>}},
    {"protocol":"apt","path":"pool/main/c/capturepkg/capturepkg_1.0.0-1_amd64.deb","descriptor":{"mediaType":"application/vnd.debian.binary-package","digest":"sha256:<deb>","size":<n>}},

    {"protocol":"pacman","path":"capture.db","descriptor":{"mediaType":"application/octet-stream","digest":"sha256:<pacman-db>","size":<n>}},
    {"protocol":"pacman","path":"capture.db.sig","descriptor":{"mediaType":"application/pgp-signature","digest":"sha256:<pacman-db-sig>","size":<n>}},
    {"protocol":"pacman","path":"capturepkg-1.0.0-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst","descriptor":{"mediaType":"application/zstd","digest":"sha256:<pacman-package>","size":<n>}}
  ]
}
```

The fixture may add `Release`/`Release.gpg`, RPM `repomd.xml.asc`, pacman package `.sig`, PyPI `.metadata`/`.asc`, and APT by-hash/extra compression routes only when its asserted client scenario needs them. Any added native reference must be a same-public-base canonical map path. `InRelease` is an ASCII clear-signed Release representation; fixture media-type selection must preserve its bytes and be declared by the publisher—the proxy only relays the descriptor media type.

### Expected client-facing mappings

| Client operation | Client-visible path | Required exact OCI blob endpoint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pip download capturepkg` project discovery | `/r/v1/YWNtZS9maXh0dXJl/pypi/simple/capturepkg/` | `/v2/acme/fixture/blobs/sha256:<pypi-project>` |
| pip wheel download | `/r/v1/YWNtZS9maXh0dXJl/pypi/packages/capturepkg-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl` | `/v2/acme/fixture/blobs/sha256:<wheel>` |
| `dnf5 makecache` | `/r/v1/YWNtZS9maXh0dXJl/rpm/repodata/repomd.xml` then exact `primary.xml.gz` | same-repo repomd and primary descriptors |
| `dnf5 download capturepkg` | `/r/v1/YWNtZS9maXh0dXJl/rpm/packages/capturepkg-1.0.0-1.x86_64.rpm` | same-repo RPM descriptor |
| `apt-get update` | `/r/v1/YWNtZS9maXh0dXJl/apt/dists/stable/InRelease` and declared Packages index | same-repo metadata descriptors |
| `apt-get download capturepkg` | `/r/v1/YWNtZS9maXh0dXJl/apt/pool/main/c/capturepkg/capturepkg_1.0.0-1_amd64.deb` | same-repo DEB descriptor |
| `pacman -Syy` | `/r/v1/YWNtZS9maXh0dXJl/pacman/capture.db` (+ `.sig` if enabled) | same-repo DB descriptors |
| `pacman -Sw capturepkg` | `/r/v1/YWNtZS9maXh0dXJl/pacman/capturepkg-1.0.0-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst` | same-repo package descriptor |

For all successful anonymous GETs, fixture expectations are `200`, descriptor `Content-Type` and exact `Content-Length`, strong digest ETag, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=0, must-revalidate, no-transform`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, and byte-identical body. For authenticated requests expect the same content semantics plus `Cache-Control: private, no-store, no-transform`. HEAD expects equivalent headers/no body. Range expects full 200/no `Accept-Ranges` in v1. Conditions use the ETag as stated in `github-oras-packages-nlf.2.3`.

### Mandatory fixture cases

| Fixture case | Expected proxy result | Upstream assertion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Valid map and each declared map route | 200/HEAD behavior as above | all paths are `/v2/acme/fixture/blobs/<declared digest>` only |
| Canonical public route mismatch (slash, query, `%2f`, dot segment, case/locator mismatch) | local 404/no-store | no upstream request |
| Unknown exact map route | local 404/no-store | no upstream request |
| Map descriptor supplies foreign repo/URL/tag/unknown field | layout rejected → 502/no-store | no foreign request |
| Duplicate `(protocol,path)`, bad sha256 spelling, wrong size, over-limit document, extra layer, OCI index, wrong config/layer type | layout rejected → 502/no-store | no mapped blob request |
| Route exists but blob 404 | 502/no-store | same-repo descriptor endpoint is requested once under retry policy |
| Blob completed length mismatch | 502 before commitment, or downstream stream abort after bytes | response never enters a shared cache |
| GHCR 401 with challenge | 401/no-store and required challenge relay | one fixed-origin request; no token-realm request |
| GHCR 403 / 429 / 5xx / timeout | 403 / 503 (+ valid Retry-After) / 502 / 504 respectively | no raw error body/header is exposed |
| Mutable tag yields new digest | snapshot keyed by new `(repo,digest)` only; optional pin rejects unapproved digest | old paths do not share blobs/ETags with new snapshot |
| Native metadata external URL, noncanonical proxy route, checksum/size mismatch, missing required sidecar | publisher validator rejects publication | proxy does not rewrite it into validity |

### Publication acceptance checks

The executable corpus must publish blobs/config/map/manifest in the specified safe order, fetch them from a GHCR-compatible fixture using both anonymous and challenge/credential cases, and exercise the four pinned client flows. It must use valid installable RPM/DEB/pacman package artifacts and signed APT/RPM/pacman metadata when an e2e test claims signature verification. The tiny non-installable capture artifacts used during initial request-shape research are not release/conformance fixtures.

### Ownership links

* `github-oras-packages-efi.2.2`: builds the real data corpus/registry fixture from this matrix.
* `github-oras-packages-nlf.2.5`: validates publisher route map/native references before publication.
* frontend e2e tasks validate package-manager behavior against the resulting corpus.
* `github-oras-packages-efi.1.2` validates the exact repository-path invariant for all entries.
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures validate schema versioning, descriptors, checksums, package metadata, and generated frontend views for each approved ecosystem.
close_reason: Published layout v1 example envelope, route-map skeleton, client-facing mappings, expected HTTP behavior, and executable valid/invalid fixture matrix for the implementation corpus.

title: Capture representative package-manager HTTP request fixtures
description: Run or collect controlled package-manager interactions for every approved ecosystem to capture request paths, headers, redirects, cache validation, range requests, and expected responses.
design:
## Captured request fixtures (sanitized)

Captured against local disposable HTTP fixture servers on 2026-09-14. The client received a per-request `Basic` challenge/credential test where supported. Transcripts record only whether authorization was present and matched a fixture value; no credential value was retained. Fixture directories are under `/tmp` and are intentionally not project artifacts. These observations must become deterministic fixture tests in `github-oras-packages-efi.2` rather than be treated as permanent implementation assets.

| Package type | Captured client/version | Discovery/refresh request path(s) | Archive request path | Credential observation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PyPI | pip 25.1.1 / CPython 3.14.7 on Fedora 43 | `GET /simple/capturepkg/`, then incidental `GET /simple/pip/`; request `Accept` prefers `application/vnd.pypi.simple.v1+json` with HTML fallback. | `GET /packages/capturepkg-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl` after a PEP 503 HTML link with `#sha256=…`; the successful `pip download` confirms archive retrieval. | Authorization was present and matched the local Basic fixture for index and archive paths. |
| RPM | dnf5 5.2.18.0 / libdnf on Fedora 43 | `GET /repodata/repomd.xml`, then `GET /repodata/primary.xml.gz`; a minimal rpm-md fixture completed `dnf5 makecache`. | `GET /packages/capturepkg-1.0.0-1.x86_64.rpm`; `dnf5 download` completed against the descriptor advertised in primary metadata. | Authorization was present and matched the fixture for all captured requests. |
| Debian/APT | apt 3.0.3 in `debian:13-slim` (image digest `sha256:d7e12182ce18b85b93007c1dedf31f2d29e01ccf3182cc4017c709b6259bc132`) | `GET /dists/stable/InRelease`, then `GET /dists/stable/Release`; without valid signed release metadata it probes `Packages.xz`, `.bz2`, `.lzma`, `.gz`, `.lz4`, `.zst`, and plain `Packages` for `binary-amd64`/`binary-all`. In a deliberately insecure local `trusted=yes` fixture with no Release, it reached `Packages.gz`. | `GET /pool/main/c/capturepkg/capturepkg_1.0.0-1_amd64.deb`; a local `apt-get download` completed when this file was named by the package index. | Authorization was present and matched the fixture on all captured metadata and archive requests. |
| Arch/pacman | pacman 7.1.0 / libalpm 16.0.1 in `archlinux:latest` (image digest `sha256:204e91950fd364961088a01773eee9012243b7e965fed42b1d82d12416190782`) | `GET /capture.db`; a gzip tar sync database fixture allowed `pacman -Syy`. | `GET /capturepkg-1.0.0-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst`; `pacman -Sw capturepkg` completed. | pacman first attempted each request without Basic auth, received the fixture 401, then retried with credentials; the retry matched the fixture. This confirms the adapter must faithfully relay `WWW-Authenticate` rather than assume preemptive credentials. |

## Fixture behavior and limitations

* The PyPI, rpm-md, and pacman fixture paths performed successful discovery plus download. The APT fixture performed successful `apt-get download` only in an explicitly insecure local mode with absent Release metadata; it was used to capture the index/archive request sequence, **not** to satisfy the production APT signing requirement.
* Capture fixture content used tiny locally generated packages; RPM, DEB, and pacman payload bytes were intentionally inert because the objective was HTTP request shape and archive retrieval, not package installation. Future end-to-end work must use valid installable package fixtures.
* Range and conditional request paths were not triggered by these small first-download scenarios. The common transport work must test `Range`, `If-None-Match`, and `If-Modified-Since` directly with a programmable upstream fixture.
* Failure evidence: local 404 responses caused pip/project resolution failure, repeated dnf `repomd.xml` retries, APT fallback across index compression formats, and pacman database retrieval failure. The pacman 401→authorized retry was observed on both DB and archive paths.

## Implementer implications

1. Route matching must accept the captured canonical paths and project/package naming forms while keeping the selected OCI repository as a separate opaque context.
2. Forward authorization to the OCI upstream and relay `WWW-Authenticate`; do not log it.
3. Keep APT `InRelease` / `Release` / `Release.gpg` and all compression choices configurable/fixture-tested. Production support still requires valid signed Release or InRelease metadata according to `apt-secure(8)`.
4. Pin the exact e2e client image/tool versions (not only floating tags) in CI once the fixture harness is implemented.
acceptance_criteria: Sanitized fixtures contain representative discovery, metadata refresh, archive download, authentication challenge, and missing-object exchanges for each approved protocol.
close_reason: Captured sanitized local request fixtures for PyPI, dnf5, apt, and pacman, including archive flows and credential/challenge behavior; documented limitations and follow-on test requirements.
